sources.citation: Santandrea, Stefano. 1948. Little known tribes of the Bahr el Ghazal basin. Sudan Notes and Records 29(1): 78ff. (Huma material pp. 96-97).
sources.note: Nothing. Gives a short Bodo-Huma comparative wordlist and a few phrases (notes taken at Mupoi 1933); the only phonetic remark concerns b/v interchange in Bodo. No mention of stress, accent or tone for Huma.

sources.citation: Sudan Notes and Records 29(2), 1948 (whole part, scanned text).
sources.note: No Huma language material; only a book review mentioning Santandrea.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1922. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vol. 2. Oxford: Clarendon Press. (Group II Wele-Aruwimi, pp. 124-125 on Homa 151a.)
sources.note: Only says Homa phonology 'seems at first sight very aberrant' because prefixes become suffixes whose vowel is dropped 'in clipped pronunciation', so roots appear consonant-final; no statement about stress or accent placement.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vol. 1. Oxford: Clarendon Press. (Homa = language no. 151a; vocabulary and notes pp. ~497ff.)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent; vocabulary (collected 1916 by C. Christy) plus notes on location and prefixes.
